raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

On ROCm, `top_p_renorm_probs` uses the Triton renorm in `renorm_triton.py`: `torch.sort` +
`torch.cumsum` + `searchsorted` find the pivot, then Triton kernels mask, reduce and normalize with
FlashInfer's threshold semantics (ties at the pivot kept). EAGLE rejection-sampling verify calls it
every step with `bs * (k + 1)` rows. At a 154880 vocabulary on MI355X the pivot search takes most of
the ~0.7 ms per verify.

When this path runs:

- ROCm with EAGLE / MTP speculative decoding. On HIP, `--speculative-use-rejection-sampling` is turned
  on by default (otherwise verify ignores temperature and top_p), except when
  `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN` is set.
- The request samples: temperature > 0 and top_p < 1. GLM-5.2's `generation_config.json` defaults to
  temperature 1.0 / top_p 0.95, so chat and agentic clients that do not set sampling parameters take
  this path.
- Requests with temperature 0 do not run top-p in verify, so `bench_serving` with its default
  settings does not show any difference.

## Modifications

- `topp_radix_triton.py`: a radix select that returns the same pivot,
  `pivot = min{v in row : sum(x <= v) >= 1 - p}`. Probabilities are non-negative, so their fp32 bit
  patterns order like the values. The pivot is found 4 bits per pass from per-block partial bin masses
  (no fp32 atomics), with each pass's digit selection fused into the next: 9 launches for the pivot,
  about 13 for the whole renorm, many blocks per row, nothing vocabulary-sized materialized. When
  `1 - p <= 0` it returns 0.0, which keeps every entry, the same kept set as the sort path.
- `top_p_renorm_probs_triton` takes the pivot from it when `SGLANG_TOPP_RADIX=1`; the masking and
  normalization kernels are unchanged.
- `SGLANG_TOPP_RADIX` in `environ.py`, default off. With it unset nothing changes.
- Tests in `test_renorm.py`.

## Accuracy Tests

- The tests check the pivot against its definition in fp64 (1e-6 tolerance) on random, softmax,
  one-hot, all-equal, sparse-with-ties and tiny (1e-30) rows, top_p from 1e-6 to 1.0, and run
  `top_p_renorm_probs_triton` with `SGLANG_TOPP_RADIX=1`.
- On near-uniform rows the fp32 cdf can reach `1 - p` within rounding, so different fp32 summation
  orders may pick adjacent values; the fp64 definition check does not depend on summation order.
- Real verify-time inputs (GLM-5.2, GSM8K sampled, 300 calls, 3498 rows with top_p < 1): the kept set
  matches an fp64 reference on every row for both the sort path and radix, and the same uniform draw
  picks the same token on every row.
- GSM8K, 1319 questions, on `amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4` (MI355X), TP4, EAGLE 3/1/4, `sgl-eval` 0.1.2 with
  thinking on and `--max-tokens 16384`, three runs per arm, sampled at temperature 1.0 / top_p 0.95:

  | `SGLANG_TOPP_RADIX` | score (3 runs) | mean | truncated_rate |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|
  | 0 | 0.9712 / 0.9674 / 0.9712 | 0.9699 | 0.0045-0.0053 |
  | 1 | 0.9644 / 0.9727 / 0.9682 | 0.9684 | 0.0076 |

  The difference between the means (0.0015) is smaller than the spread across runs within one
  setting (up to 0.0083).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Kernel

MI355X, this commit, 154880 vocabulary, top_p 0.95. Time of `top_p_renorm_probs_triton`: GPU
kernel time from the profiler, and wall time of an isolated call.

| rows | sort path GPU / wall | radix GPU / wall | saved per call (wall) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 (bs 1 x 4) | 676 / 682 us | 69 / 181 us | 0.50 ms |
| 16 (bs 4 x 4) | 674 / 651 us | 145 / 180 us | 0.47 ms |
| 32 (bs 8 x 4) | 837 / 815 us | 222 / 258 us | 0.56 ms |
| 64 (bs 16 x 4) | 1175 / 1158 us | 420 / 458 us | 0.70 ms |
| 128 (bs 32 x 4) | 4327 / 4339 us | 777 / 811 us | 3.5 ms |
| 256 (bs 64 x 4) | 4605 / 4627 us | 1549 / 1585 us | 3.0 ms |

At small row counts the radix wall time is bounded by its ~13 launches (~180 us).

### End to end

`amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4`, MI355X TP4, image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.21-rocm10-mi35x-20261004` (sglang
`ab9d8f029c`) with this commit, EAGLE 3/1/4, rejection sampling on, `bench_serving` random
(range ratio 0.8, num-prompts = conc x 5), temperature 1.0 / top_p 0.95. Servers ran in the order
sort, radix, sort, radix; each value is the geometric mean of the two runs of its setting. TPUT is
total tok/s per GPU; TPOT is the median.

| ISL -> OSL | conc | TPUT sort | TPUT radix | TPUT delta | TPOT sort | TPOT radix | TPOT delta | ITL sort | ITL radix | ITL delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1024 -> 1024 | 4 | 352.8 | 352.4 | -0.1% | 4.72 ms | 4.67 ms | +1.1% | 4.17 ms | 4.05 ms | +3.0% |
| 1024 -> 1024 | 8 | 469.4 | 497.1 | +5.9% | 7.41 ms | 7.01 ms | +5.4% | 5.89 ms | 5.70 ms | +3.2% |
| 1024 -> 1024 | 16 | 720.2 | 770.9 | +7.0% | 9.48 ms | 8.53 ms | +10.0% | 7.10 ms | 6.91 ms | +2.7% |
| 1024 -> 1024 | 32 | 1125.2 | 1136.3 | +1.0% | 11.81 ms | 11.48 ms | +2.8% | 9.11 ms | 8.74 ms | +4.1% |
| 1024 -> 1024 | 64 | 1401.3 | 1442.4 | +2.9% | 14.44 ms | 14.24 ms | +1.4% | 10.90 ms | 10.56 ms | +3.1% |
| 1024 -> 1024 | geomean | | | +3.3% | | | +4.2% | | | +3.2% |
| 8192 -> 1024 | 4 | 1451.0 | 1527.8 | +5.3% | 5.33 ms | 5.17 ms | +2.9% | 4.22 ms | 4.09 ms | +3.0% |
| 8192 -> 1024 | 8 | 1994.4 | 1999.1 | +0.2% | 8.21 ms | 8.00 ms | +2.6% | 5.74 ms | 5.59 ms | +2.5% |
| 8192 -> 1024 | 16 | 2697.1 | 2665.8 | -1.2% | 12.13 ms | 12.03 ms | +0.9% | 7.03 ms | 6.86 ms | +2.5% |
| 8192 -> 1024 | 32 | 3358.5 | 3424.5 | +2.0% | 19.33 ms | 19.10 ms | +1.2% | 9.10 ms | 8.73 ms | +4.1% |
| 8192 -> 1024 | 64 | 3687.5 | 3725.8 | +1.0% | 27.34 ms | 27.04 ms | +1.1% | 11.00 ms | 10.65 ms | +3.1% |
| 8192 -> 1024 | geomean | | | +1.5% | | | +1.7% | | | +3.0% |
| 70000 -> 300 | 4 | 4672.1 | 4682.6 | +0.2% | 29.71 ms | 27.17 ms | +8.5% | 4.24 ms | 4.13 ms | +2.7% |
| 70000 -> 300 | 8 | 4799.2 | 4804.2 | +0.1% | 64.19 ms | 69.83 ms | -8.8% | 5.60 ms | 5.46 ms | +2.5% |
| 70000 -> 300 | 16 | 4844.3 | 4851.8 | +0.2% | 72.48 ms | 73.82 ms | -1.8% | 5.67 ms | 5.56 ms | +2.1% |
| 70000 -> 300 | 32 | 4854.9 | 4853.7 | -0.0% | 79.01 ms | 76.49 ms | +3.2% | 5.75 ms | 5.60 ms | +2.7% |
| 70000 -> 300 | 64 | 4833.0 | 4841.8 | +0.2% | 77.78 ms | 78.38 ms | -0.8% | 5.79 ms | 5.66 ms | +2.1% |
| 70000 -> 300 | geomean | | | +0.1% | | | +0.2% | | | +2.4% |

TPUT delta is how much higher radix is; TPOT delta and ITL delta are how much lower radix is. ITL is the median.

- Accept length is the same in both settings (geomean ratio 0.997-1.001).
- TPUT and TPOT move with the accept length of each run, so they are noisy: between the two runs of
  the same setting TPUT differs by up to 6% and TPOT by up to 9%. At 70000 -> 300 TPOT is dominated
  by the prefill of other requests and differs by up to 8.6% between the two sort runs.
- Median ITL follows the per-round time and is stable: the two runs of the same setting are within
  1%. It is lower with radix in every cell (2.1-4.1%).
- The 8192 -> 1024 conc 4 profile with `SGLANG_TOPP_RADIX=1` shows `top_p_pivots_radix` on every
  verify step and no sort kernel.

## Checklist

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).

files.patch:
@@ -8,6 +8,8 @@
 import triton
 import triton.language as tl
 
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+
 _BLOCK_SIZE = 1024
 
 
@@ -96,7 +98,9 @@ def top_p_renorm_probs_triton(
 
     Sorting and prefix sums use PyTorch's device kernels because a vocabulary-sized
     in-register Triton sort does not scale to 100K+ vocabularies. Triton performs
-    the bandwidth-heavy masking, partial reduction, and normalization.
+    the bandwidth-heavy masking, partial reduction, and normalization. With
+    SGLANG_TOPP_RADIX=1 the pivot comes from the sort-free radix select in
+    topp_radix_triton.py instead.
     """
     probs_fp32 = _prepare_probs(probs)
     batch_size, vocab_size = probs_fp32.shape
@@ -119,6 +123,11 @@ def top_p_renorm_probs_triton(
             (batch_size,), float(top_p), device=probs.device, dtype=torch.float32
         )
 
+    if envs.SGLANG_TOPP_RADIX.get():
+        from sglang.kernels.ops.sampling.topp_radix_triton import top_p_pivots_radix
+
+        return _renorm_from_pivots(probs_fp32, top_p_pivots_radix(probs_fp32, top_ps))
+
     # Match FlashInfer's threshold semantics: sort ascending, discard the prefix
     # whose cumulative mass is below 1 - p, and retain all ties at the pivot.
     sorted_probs = torch.sort(probs_fp32, dim=-1).values

@@ -0,0 +1,163 @@
+"""Sort-free top-p pivot for ROCm: mass-weighted radix select over fp32 bit patterns.
+
+Reference semantics (sglang top_p_renorm_probs_triton / FlashInfer): sort ascending,
+cdf = cumsum, cutoff = first index with cdf >= 1 - p, pivot = sorted[cutoff], keep x >= pivot.
+Equivalently pivot = min{v in row : G(v) >= 1 - p}, G(v) = sum of x with x <= v. Probs are
+non-negative, so their fp32 bit patterns order like the values; the pivot's bit pattern is
+found BITS bits at a time. When 1 - p <= 0 the search returns 0.0, which keeps every
+entry (the reference returns the row minimum; the kept set is the same).
+
+Pass p (one launch over (rows, blocks)) first finishes the digit selection of pass p - 1:
+every program sums the previous pass's per-block partial bin masses (a few hundred floats)
+and derives (prefix, mass below prefix); block 0 stores that state for pass p + 1. Then it
+writes its own partial bin masses for elements matching the prefix. Partials are stored per
+block instead of accumulated with fp32 atomics, which contend badly on ROCm. A final
+single-block-per-row launch selects the last digit: PASSES + 1 launches in total.
+"""
+
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+_BLOCK = 4096
+_BITS = 4
+_BINS = 1 << _BITS
+_PASSES = 32 // _BITS
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _select(
+    part_ptr,
+    state_ptr,
+    target,
+    row,
+    rows,
+    NBLK,
+    P: tl.constexpr,
+    NBLK_P2: tl.constexpr,
+    BINS: tl.constexpr,
+    BITS: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    """Digit selection for pass P from its partials and the state left by pass P - 1."""
+    bins = tl.arange(0, BINS)
+    blks = tl.arange(0, NBLK_P2)
+    ptrs = part_ptr + ((P * rows + row) * NBLK + blks[:, None]) * BINS + bins[None, :]
+    h = tl.sum(tl.load(ptrs, mask=blks[:, None] < NBLK, other=0.0), axis=0)
+    if P > 0:
+        prefix = tl.load(state_ptr + (P - 1) * rows * 2 + row * 2).to(
+            tl.int32, bitcast=True
+        )
+        below = tl.load(state_ptr + (P - 1) * rows * 2 + row * 2 + 1)
+    else:
+        prefix = tl.zeros((), dtype=tl.int32)
+        below = tl.zeros((), dtype=tl.float32)
+    cum = below + tl.cumsum(h, axis=0)
+    first_ok = tl.min(tl.where(cum >= target, bins, BINS), axis=0)

+    probs_ptr,
+    part_ptr,
+    state_ptr,
+    target_ptr,

+    NBLK,
+    PASS: tl.constexpr,
+    NBLK_P2: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+    BINS: tl.constexpr,
+    BITS: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    row = tl.program_id(0)
+    blk = tl.program_id(1)
+    rows = tl.num_programs(0)
+    shift_hi: tl.constexpr = 32 - BITS * PASS

+    x = tl.load(probs_ptr + base + offs, mask=m, other=0.0)
+    if PASS > 0:

+        if blk == 0:

+@triton.jit
+def _final_kernel(
+    part_ptr,
+    state_ptr,
+    target_ptr,
+    pivot_ptr,
+    NBLK,
+    PASSES: tl.constexpr,
+    NBLK_P2: tl.constexpr,
+    BINS: tl.constexpr,
+    BITS: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    row = tl.program_id(0)
+    rows = tl.num_programs(0)
+    target = tl.load(target_ptr + row)
+    prefix, below = _select(
+        part_ptr, state_ptr, target, row, rows, NBLK, PASSES - 1, NBLK_P2, BINS, BITS
+    )
+    tl.store(pivot_ptr + row, prefix)

+def top_p_pivots_radix(probs_fp32: torch.Tensor, top_ps: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    rows, V = probs_fp32.shape
+    dev = probs_fp32.device
+    bits = probs_fp32.view(torch.int32)
+    target = (1.0 - top_ps.to(torch.float32)).contiguous()
+    nblk = triton.cdiv(V, _BLOCK)
+    nblk_p2 = triton.next_power_of_2(nblk)
+    part = torch.empty((_PASSES, rows, nblk, _BINS), device=dev, dtype=torch.float32)
+    state = torch.empty((_PASSES, rows, 2), device=dev, dtype=torch.float32)
+    for p in range(_PASSES):
+        _pass_kernel[(rows, nblk)](
+            bits,
+            probs_fp32,
+            part,
+            state,
+            target,
+            V,
+            nblk,
+            PASS=p,
+            NBLK_P2=nblk_p2,
+            BLOCK=_BLOCK,
+            BINS=_BINS,
+            BITS=_BITS,
+            num_warps=8,
+        )
+    pivot = torch.empty(rows, device=dev, dtype=torch.int32)
+    _final_kernel[(rows,)](
+        part,
+        state,
+        target,
+        pivot,
+        nblk,
+        PASSES=_PASSES,
+        NBLK_P2=nblk_p2,
+        BINS=_BINS,
+        BITS=_BITS,
+    )
+    return pivot.view(torch.float32)

+def _make_probs(kind, batch_size, vocab_size):
+    g = torch.Generator(device="cuda:0").manual_seed(42)
+    if kind == "uniform_rand":
+        x = torch.rand(batch_size, vocab_size, device="cuda:0", generator=g)
+        return x / x.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
+    if kind.startswith("softmax"):
+        scale = float(kind.split("_")[1])
+        logits = torch.randn(batch_size, vocab_size, device="cuda:0", generator=g)
+        return torch.softmax(logits * scale, dim=-1)
+    if kind == "one_hot":
+        x = torch.zeros(batch_size, vocab_size, device="cuda:0")
+        x[:, 0] = 1.0
+        return x
+    if kind == "all_equal":
+        return torch.full((batch_size, vocab_size), 1.0 / vocab_size, device="cuda:0")
+    if kind == "sparse_ties":
+        x = torch.randint(0, 4, (batch_size, vocab_size), device="cuda:0", generator=g)
+        x = x.float()
+        x[:, 0] += 1.0
+        return x / x.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
+    if kind == "tiny":
+        x = torch.rand(batch_size, vocab_size, device="cuda:0", generator=g) * 1e-30
+        return x
+    raise ValueError(kind)
+
+
+def _check_pivot_definition(probs, top_ps, pivots, eps=1e-6):
+    """pivot = min{v in row : sum(x <= v) >= 1 - p}, checked in fp64 on the row values."""
+    x = probs.double()
+    target = (1.0 - top_ps.double()).unsqueeze(1)
+    v = pivots.double().unsqueeze(1)
+    # With 1 - p <= 0 every entry is kept; the pivot may then be 0 rather than a row value.
+    keep_all = (target <= 0).squeeze(1)
+    assert bool((x[keep_all] >= v[keep_all]).all()), "top_p >= 1 must keep every entry"
+    x, target, v = x[~keep_all], target[~keep_all], v[~keep_all]
+    if x.shape[0] == 0:
+        return
+    assert bool((x == v).any(dim=1).all()), "pivot must be a value of its row"
+    mass_le = torch.where(x <= v, x, 0.0).sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)
+    below = (
+        torch.where(x < v, x, torch.full_like(x, -1.0)).max(dim=1, keepdim=True).values
+    )
+    mass_le_below = torch.where(x <= below, x, 0.0).sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)
+    has_below = below >= 0
+    total = x.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)
+    reaches = (mass_le >= target - eps) | (v == x.max(dim=1, keepdim=True).values)
+    minimal = (
+        ~has_below | (mass_le_below < target + eps) | (target <= 0) | (total < target)
+    )
+    assert bool(reaches.all()), "kept mass below the top_p budget"
+    assert bool(minimal.all()), "a smaller pivot would already reach the budget"
+
